run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T15:50:07Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend is explained by a broken cart data-store dependency. The valkey-cart Deployment's only container runs with a 10Mi memory limit (requests 4Mi, the smallest memory limit among the 21 otel-demo Deployments); its pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft has restartCount 4, is not ready, and its last terminated state is reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 at 2026-11-16T15:53:06Z, leaving it in CrashLoopBackOff. Kubelet BackOff warning events for that pod run from 15:50:05Z (two seconds before the alert start 15:50:07Z) to 15:57:23Z, and the valkey-cart Deployment reports Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable) with unavailableReplicas 1. The valkey-cart Service endpoints contain only a notReadyAddress for that pod, and the cart Deployment is configured with VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, so cart logs repeat "Wasn't able to connect to redis". Cart's own error spans appear on CartService/AddItem, GetCart and EmptyCart, checkout's errors are on CartService calls and PlaceOrder, and frontend's own error spans concentrate on /api/cart, /api/checkout, grpc CartService/AddItem and GetCart, and PlaceOrder; frontend's error-span fraction rose from 0 to ~8.5% between 15:51:07Z and 15:59:07Z, matching the alert onset. Node memory pressure and a traffic surge were checked and rejected. The exact alert expression could not be verified because this Prometheus holds no alerting rules, and Jaeger has no traces after 15:29:08Z, so span-level error details and valkey's own logs for the failure window are gaps.

claims.text: frontend emitted error spans throughout the window: sum by status_code of increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend"}[4727s]) returned STATUS_CODE_ERROR 782.62 and STATUS_CODE_UNSET 90006.72 over 2026-11-16T14:50:07Z-16:08:54Z.

frontend's error-span fraction was 0 from 15:42:07Z through 15:49:07Z, then 0.00219 at 15:51:07Z, 0.00993 at 15:53:07Z, 0.05049 at 15:55:07Z, 0.05859 at 15:57:07Z and 0.08511 at 15:59:07Z (last point; metric samples ended 16:01:07Z), i.e. the rise begins at the alert start 15:50:07Z.

frontend's error spans are concentrated on cart/checkout-dependent operations: increase over the window was GET /api/cart 56.92, POST /api/cart 151.44, executing api route (pages) /api/cart 208.36, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 122.98, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 85.38, POST /api/checkout 32.52, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 32.52 and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 32.52 (GET 21.34, POST 38.62).

The cart service itself produced error spans: POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 124.75, POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 103.94 and POST /oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart 1.125 in the window, and cart's error-span rate rose from 0 before 15:46:07Z to 0.0158/s at 15:51:07Z and 0.53/s at 15:53:07Z.

cart pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 logs the line "Wasn't able to connect to redis" repeatedly together with "Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised." from 15:55:54Z through the newest matching line at 15:57:30Z (100 newest of 324 matching lines).

The cart Deployment's container env sets VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, and the valkey-cart Service (ClusterIP 100.65.106.169, port 6379, selector opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart) has an Endpoints object whose only subset holds a notReadyAddresses entry for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft; there is no ready address for the cart backend.

Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft (startTime 2026-11-16T15:12:27Z) has container valkey-cart with ready=false, restartCount=4, state waiting/reason CrashLoopBackOff ("back-off 1m20s restarting failed container"), and lastState terminated with reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, startedAt 15:52:55Z, finishedAt 15:53:06Z; pod condition Ready=False/ContainersNotReady since 15:53:06Z.

The valkey-cart Deployment (created 15:12:27Z, generation 1, observedGeneration 1) runs image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine with resources limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi and requests cpu 2m / memory 4Mi; 10Mi is the smallest memory limit among the 21 otel-demo Deployments (next smallest is image-provider and shipping at 15Mi).

The valkey-cart Deployment reports Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable ("Deployment does not have minimum availability") since 15:53:06Z, unavailableReplicas 1, and its ReplicaSet valkey-cart-58df56c79c (owner Deployment valkey-cart) has replicas 1 with readyReplicas null, while cart's ReplicaSet cart-755465879b reports readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1.

Kubelet Warning events for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft show reason BackOff with count 22, firstTimestamp 2026-11-16T15:50:05Z and lastTimestamp 2026-11-16T15:57:23Z; 15:50:05Z is two seconds before the alert's stated start 15:50:07Z and the frontend error rise at 15:51:07Z.

checkout also produced its own error spans on cart-dependent operations: oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 31.9, HTTP POST 14.3, oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 17.6 and oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart 1.125 in the window.
frontend-proxy produced its own error spans in the same window: span_name ingress 580.21 and router frontend egress 58.94.

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running at query time and every container reported restarts 0 except valkey-cart (ready=false, restartCount 4); cart-755465879b-4p8d9, frontend-675fd7b5c5-x9gbm, checkout-5dccddf8bb-2ktmw and the rest were ready.

The two error-span series returned for accounting and payment were both 0 over the window (increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}), so neither showed its own error spans.

All 21 otel-demo pods were created within a three-second span at 15:12:27Z-15:12:30Z (valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft at 15:12:27Z), so the pod that later OOM-looped had been running about 38 minutes before the BackOff events started at 15:50:05Z.

Sampled cgroup memory does not show the 10Mi limit being reached: max_over_time(container_memory_max_usage_bytes) for the valkey-cart container instances peaked at 5,582,848 bytes, container_memory_failcnt was 0 for every instance, and pod-level container_memory_working_set_bytes reached only 7,147,520 bytes at 16:08:54Z against a 10,485,760-byte limit; the fatal spike therefore lies between samples and the OOM attribution rests on the kubelet-recorded OOMKilled reason rather than on an observed limit breach.

Primary chain: the valkey-cart container's 10Mi memory limit is too small for valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine, so the container is OOMKilled repeatedly (exitCode 137), the pod never becomes ready, valkey-cart has no ready endpoint, cart cannot reach its required VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 store, cart returns gRPC errors on GetCart/AddItem/EmptyCart, and frontend's cart and checkout API routes plus its grpc client spans error, driving the alert.

Secondary detail: the OOM onset at ~15:50Z after ~38 minutes of uptime is consistent with gradual valkey memory growth crossing the small 10Mi limit (observed working set grew from ~3.5MB to ~4.3MB between 15:26Z and 15:33Z and the newest container instance was at ~7.1MB by 16:08:54Z), rather than an instantaneous configuration change.

Node-level memory pressure as the OOM cause is rejected: all five nodes report MemoryPressure status False with reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory and Ready True, and the other pods on the valkey-cart node i-0d211959f7bf532cd (e.g. cart-755465879b-4p8d9, checkout-5dccddf8bb-2ktmw, frontend is on i-011a5a806da9fd225) show restartCount 0.

A traffic surge into cart as the trigger is not supported: cart's span rate was flat at 14.75-17.20 spans/s from 15:32:07Z to 15:53:07Z, the highest reading (17.2/s at 15:39:07Z) precedes onset, and the rate then fell to 11.75/s at 15:51:07Z, 6.68/s at 15:53:07Z and 3.08/s at 15:55:07Z as failures accumulated.

The small error-span counts on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation are not this cause: they occur only on flagd stream operations (ad flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 2.04, fraud-detection flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 3.05, recommendation /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 3.05, with ResolveBoolean/ResolveInt 0), which is a different operation class from the cart/checkout path and is not tied to the frontend request failures.

Raise the valkey-cart Deployment container memory limit (and matching request) from the current 10Mi/4Mi to a value with headroom above valkey's working set, comparable to the other stateful datastores in the namespace (postgresql 100Mi limit/50Mi request), then confirm the pod leaves CrashLoopBackOff and valkey-cart endpoints regain a ready address; verify afterwards that cart stops logging "Wasn't able to connect to redis" and that frontend's /api/cart and /api/checkout error spans stop.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alert rule is not present in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules filtered by rule_name=RequestErrorRate and by type=alert both returned no_data, so the alert's exact expression, threshold and the metric behind the reported current value 3.0222 could not be verified.

The target exposes no http_server_request_duration_seconds_count or rpc_client/rpc_server_duration_milliseconds series (metric-name discovery for those names returned nothing); only traces_span_metrics_calls_total, container_*/redis_*/node metrics and kube_* state metrics exist, so the request-level error-rate metric the alert evaluates is unknown, and span counts are not request counts.

Jaeger has no trace data after 2026-11-16T15:29:08Z: traces_search for frontend over 14:50:07Z-16:08:54Z returned newest spans at 15:29:05-15:29:08, and searches for cart over 15:50:00Z-16:08:54Z and frontend over 15:55:00Z-16:08:54Z returned no traces at all, so error-span status codes and error text for the failure window are unavailable.

valkey-cart's own logs could not be read: the current container never started (CrashLoopBackOff) and the previous container instance was reported as not found, so valkey's OOM diagnostics are unknown.
frontend-675fd7b5c5-x9gbm container logs for 15:45:00Z-16:08:54Z returned zero lines, so frontend-side error messages could not be read or used to confirm or clear frontend as a contributing fault.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so whether the 10Mi memory limit was introduced or changed at the 15:12:27Z namespace-wide pod rollout cannot be verified; pod and Deployment objects only show current state.

cAdvisor samples do not capture the fatal memory spike: per-container max usage peaked at 5,582,848 bytes and container_memory_failcnt stayed 0 against the 10,485,760-byte limit, so the exact allocation that triggered the kernel OOM kill is unobserved.

Warning event series for cart-9fd895bb7-m7zfz (reason FailedKillPod, count 22, first 2026-11-15T03:15:02Z, last 2026-11-16T15:47:55Z) refers to a cart pod that no longer exists (current cart pod is cart-755465879b-4p8d9); it ended shortly before onset but could not be tied to this incident and remains unexplained.
Metric samples for traces_span_metrics_calls_total end at 16:01:07Z (about 8 minutes before the window end 16:08:54Z), so the last part of the window has no span-metric evidence.

No redis_* memory series exists for valkey-cart (the only redis_memory_used_bytes series returned belongs to pod otel-collector-564d9c7987-sht2q), so valkey's internal memory growth could not be measured directly.
next_steps: Review the valkey-cart Deployment manifest and any recent Helm/values changes that set resources.limits.memory=10Mi, using the change-history system outside this Run, to confirm when the limit was introduced.

After raising the memory limit, watch valkey-cart pod restart count, container_memory_working_set_bytes against the new limit, valkey-cart Endpoints ready addresses, and cart log lines containing "Wasn't able to connect to redis".

Re-check the alerting rule source (Alertmanager/recording-rule repository) for the RequestErrorRate expression to confirm which metric and threshold produced current 3.0222, since that rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus.
Confirm with the Jaeger/collector owner why trace ingestion stops around 15:29Z so that error-span details are available for post-incident review.
Investigate why cart-9fd895bb7-m7zfz logged FailedKillPod warnings through 15:47:55Z if that workload is still expected to exist or be cleaned up.
